# DCPROSENS — Full Reference Dataset (LLM-optimized)
> https://dcprosens.com
> Last updated: 2026-11-22 | 87 games | 570 articles | 18 Field Guides | Licence: cite with attribution to https://dcprosens.com

This is the complete, expanded reference dataset behind DCPROSENS's sensitivity converter — every supported game with its engine, category, sourced yaw value, and sourcing notes. See https://dcprosens.com/llms.txt for a shorter summary and the full tool list.

All yaw values represent degrees of camera rotation per raw mouse count at sensitivity 1.0, used in: cm/360 = (360 x 2.54) / (yaw x sensitivity x DPI). Games are never added to this list without a real, checkable source (engine confirmation or a published technical constant) — entries explicitly marked unverified/approximation should be treated with more caution than the rest.

## Full Game Dataset (87 games)

### Valorant
- id: valorant
- yaw: 0.07
- engine: Unreal Engine 4 (Riot custom netcode)
- category: Tactical Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/valorant/
- notes: Valorant uses the highest yaw value (0.07) of any major competitive shooter, meaning the smallest physical mouse movement produces the most camera rotation. That is why Valorant sensitivity numbers look tiny (0.2-0.5) compared to CS2 or Apex.

### CS2
- id: csgo
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source 2
- category: Tactical Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/csgo/
- notes: CS2 runs on Source 2, the successor to the original Source engine that also powers Apex Legends and (partially) Deadlock — which is why those three share the same 0.022 yaw and convert 1:1 at the same DPI.

### Apex Legends
- id: apex
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source (modified, Respawn)
- category: Battle Royale
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/apex/
- notes: Apex Legends runs on a heavily modified Source engine, inheriting the same 0.022 yaw as CS2. The extra layer to manage is ADS sensitivity per scope (1x-4x), which Apex treats as separate multipliers rather than a single zoom slider.

### Overwatch 2
- id: overwatch
- yaw: 0.0066
- engine: Proprietary (Blizzard)
- category: Hero Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/overwatch/
- notes: Overwatch 2 uses a yaw of 0.0066, the same family as Call of Duty and Destiny 2. Because heroes have wildly different zoom levels (Ana's scope, Widowmaker's sniper, Sombra's hip-fire), Overwatch also has a separate "Relative Aim Sensitivity While Zoomed" slider most converters ignore.

### Fortnite
- id: fortnite
- yaw: 0.005555
- engine: Unreal Engine 5
- category: Battle Royale / Building Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/fortnite/
- notes: Fortnite has the lowest yaw (0.005555) of any game in this list, so numeric sensitivity values look large. Building adds a second layer most other games do not have: many players run a separate, higher "Builder Pro" turn rate independent of their aim sensitivity.

### Call of Duty: Warzone / MW3
- id: cod
- yaw: 0.0066
- engine: IW Engine
- category: Battle Royale / Tactical Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/cod/
- notes: Modern Call of Duty titles share a yaw of 0.0066 across Warzone, MW3, and Black Ops — the same family as Overwatch 2 and Destiny 2 — so sensitivity values transfer across CoD sub-titles without conversion.

### Rainbow Six Siege
- id: rainbow6
- yaw: 0.00572
- engine: AnvilNext 2.0 (Ubisoft)
- category: Tactical Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/rainbow6/
- notes: Siege uses one of the lower yaw values on this list (0.00572), and every operator with an ACOG or scope applies its own ADS multiplier on top of your base sensitivity — so a value that feels right hipfire can still need per-scope tuning.

### Destiny 2
- id: destiny2
- yaw: 0.0066
- engine: Proprietary Tiger Engine (Bungie)
- category: Looter Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/destiny2/
- notes: Destiny 2 shares the 0.0066 yaw family with Call of Duty and Overwatch 2, but its wide range of weapon archetypes (snipers, scout rifles, hand cannons) each carry different zoom levels, so ADS feel varies more than in flatter tactical shooters.

### Marvel Rivals
- id: marvelrivals
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Unreal Engine 5 (NetEase)
- category: Hero Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/marvelrivals/
- notes: Marvel Rivals launched on Unreal Engine 5 and settled on a 0.022 yaw, the same as CS2 and Apex Legends — a common choice for newer UE5 shooters aiming for a familiar competitive feel out of the box.

### THE FINALS
- id: thefinals
- yaw: 0.0066
- engine: Unreal Engine 5 (Embark Studios)
- category: Arena Destruction Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/thefinals/
- notes: THE FINALS uses a 0.0066 yaw, aligning it with the Call of Duty / Overwatch 2 / Destiny 2 family rather than the Source-engine 0.022 standard — worth checking explicitly if you are switching from CS2 or Apex.

### Minecraft (Java)
- id: minecraft
- yaw: 0.6
- engine: Custom Java (Mojang)
- category: Sandbox / PvP
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/minecraft/
- notes: Minecraft Java does not use a fixed yaw like FPS games — its mouse code (f = sensitivity × 0.6 + 0.2, then cubed) is non-linear, so no single conversion number is exact at every setting. The value used here approximates the 40-70% slider range most PvP players actually play in; treat the converted number as a strong starting point to fine-tune by feel, not a locked-in exact match.

### Roblox
- id: roblox
- yaw: 0.2
- engine: Custom (Roblox Engine)
- category: Platform / Multi-Genre
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/roblox/
- notes: Roblox is a platform, not a single game — camera sensitivity is set once at the platform level and carries into most first-person Roblox shooters and PvP experiences. Roblox does not publish its camera code, so the yaw used here is an approximation rather than a confirmed engine constant; use it as a starting point and adjust by feel inside the specific experience you play.

### Team Fortress 2
- id: tf2
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source
- category: Class-Based Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/tf2/
- notes: Team Fortress 2 runs on the original Source engine and uses the same 0.022 yaw as CS2, Left 4 Dead 2, and every other Source-family title — sensitivity carries over 1:1 at the same DPI with zero conversion needed.

### Left 4 Dead 2
- id: l4d2
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source
- category: Co-op Survival Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/l4d2/
- notes: Left 4 Dead 2 shares the Source engine's standard 0.022 yaw with CS2, TF2, and Half-Life-derived titles, so any sensitivity you already use in another Source game transfers over exactly.

### Titanfall 2
- id: titanfall2
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source (modified, Respawn)
- category: Movement Shooter
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/titanfall2/
- notes: Titanfall 2 runs on a heavily modified Source engine (the same lineage Respawn later used for Apex Legends) and keeps the familiar 0.022 yaw — though its fast wall-running movement means many players run a noticeably lower cm/360 than they would in a stationary tac-shooter.

### Hunt: Showdown

- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/huntshowdown/

### Grand Theft Auto V

### Half-Life 2
- id: hl2
- yaw: 0.022
- engine: Source
- category: Classic FPS
- page: https://dcprosens.com/sens-finder/hl2/
- notes: Half-Life 2 helped define the Source engine's 0.022 m_yaw convention that CS2, TF2, and dozens of other Valve and Valve-licensed titles still use today.

## Games Without a Yaw Converter (DPI Guides Instead)

These games do not use a rotating first-person camera, so a yaw-based sensitivity converter does not apply. DCPROSENS instead recommends a DPI range based on real pro-player examples.

### League of Legends
- page: https://dcprosens.com/dpi-guide/lol/
- why no converter: Camera is a fixed top-down view controlled by keyboard/edge-scroll, not mouse look. Precision comes from click-targeting, not turn rate.
- reference: Faker plays at 800 DPI.

### Dota 2
- page: https://dcprosens.com/dpi-guide/dota2/
- why no converter: Same top-down, click-to-move camera model as League of Legends — no rotating camera to convert a yaw value for.

### Free Fire
- page: https://dcprosens.com/dpi-guide/freefire/
- why no converter: Mobile touch-based aiming does not map to a desktop mouse yaw constant; DPI guidance instead targets emulator/mobile-controller setups.

## Structural Exclusions (Genres Intentionally Not Covered)

DCPROSENS does not force sensitivity conversion onto genres where the simple linear-yaw model does not apply:

- **MOBA / RTS / isometric ARPG / top-down roguelite**: camera is not mouse-rotation-controlled (League of Legends, Dota 2, Diablo-likes, Vampire Survivors-likes, Command & Conquer, Civilization).
- **Cockpit "torso-twist" mech sims**: MechWarrior, Armored Core, Hawken, and similar titles use a separate torso/turret turn-rate system, not a simple camera yaw — MechWarrior 5 is explicitly listed as unsupported by mouse-sensitivity.com for this exact reason.
- **VR titles**: head-tracking replaces mouse-look entirely (Pavlov, Onward, Half-Life: Alyx, etc.).
- **Flight-stick space sims**: Star Citizen, Elite Dangerous, and similar titles use analog flight-model input rather than a fixed degrees-per-count camera yaw.
- **Non-linear sensitivity curves**: flagged per-game rather than excluded outright (see Minecraft Java above) when a reasonable approximation is still possible.

## Conversion Formulas

- Sensitivity in Game B = Sensitivity in Game A × (Yaw_A / Yaw_B)
- eDPI = DPI × In-game Sensitivity
- cm/360 = (360 × 2.54) / (Yaw × Sensitivity × DPI)

## Sourcing Methodology

Every yaw value in this dataset was added under one of these evidence tiers, from strongest to weakest:
1. **Direct technical source** — official tool source code (e.g. KovaaK's Sensitivity Matcher GitHub repository) or a game's own published console variable documentation.
2. **Confirmed engine family** — the game's engine was verified (not assumed) to be Source, GoldSrc, or id Tech, all of which are independently and repeatedly confirmed to share the 0.022 m_yaw default.
3. **Cross-validated community source** — a converter site or public repository whose other listed values independently matched already-confirmed entries in this dataset, lending credibility to its remaining figures.
4. **Single-source figure** — explicitly flagged as such in the notes field; treat as a reasonable starting point, not a guaranteed-exact match.

Games with implausible values relative to the rest of this dataset (e.g. a figure roughly 100x every comparable entry) are rejected outright rather than included with a caveat — this has happened at least once during development (a sourced Fallout 4 figure of 3.78, next to an accepted Fallout 76 figure of 0.0175 from the same source, was excluded as an almost-certain unit error).
